category: Set up and configure Microsoft Fabric

documents.title: Choose a Fabric capacity
documents.content: A Fabric capacity supplies shared compute for Fabric workloads. Choose a trial, Fabric F SKU, or supported Power BI capacity according to workload size, concurrency, scaling, region, and cost requirements.

documents.title: Configure capacity performance
documents.content: Capacity configuration affects performance and cost. Size capacity units for expected demand, monitor throttling and utilization, and use scaling or autoscale options to respond to changing workloads.

documents.title: Create and manage workspaces
documents.content: Fabric workspaces organize related analytics items. Create a workspace, assign it to a capacity, configure its settings, and grant roles according to each user's responsibilities.

documents.title: Choose a Fabric workload
documents.content: Choose Data Factory for integration, Data Engineering for lakehouse processing, Data Warehouse for relational analytics, Real-Time Intelligence for event data, and Power BI for semantic modeling and reporting.

documents.title: Organize data in OneLake
documents.content: OneLake is the unified storage foundation for Fabric. Organize workspaces and items around business domains, ownership, environments, and governance boundaries so data is discoverable and reusable.

documents.title: Create lakehouses and warehouses
documents.content: Lakehouses combine files, Delta tables, Spark, and SQL access. Warehouses provide a relational SQL experience. Choose the item that best matches engineering, modeling, and BI needs.

documents.title: Create OneLake shortcuts
documents.content: OneLake shortcuts reference data without requiring another copy. Use shortcuts to connect Fabric items or supported external storage while considering permissions, caching, and source availability.

documents.title: Configure Power BI settings
documents.content: Fabric administrators configure tenant, capacity, workspace, sharing, export, and developer settings to balance collaboration with organizational security policies.

documents.title: Assign workspace roles
documents.content: Workspace roles control broad access to Fabric items. Assign the least privileged Admin, Member, Contributor, or Viewer role and use item-level controls for narrower access.

documents.title: Secure lakehouse and warehouse data
documents.content: Use SQL permissions, item sharing, and OneLake data access roles where supported so users can reach only the schemas, tables, folders, or rows they require.

documents.title: Implement semantic model security
documents.content: Power BI semantic models support row-level security to filter records and object-level security to hide tables or columns. Define roles carefully and test them before publication.

documents.title: Use managed identities and connections
documents.content: Prefer managed identities or organizational accounts where supported, control connection sharing, and avoid embedding credentials in notebooks, pipelines, or reports.

documents.title: Apply sensitivity labels
documents.content: Sensitivity labels classify and protect Fabric and Power BI content. Apply labels consistently so handling expectations follow supported data when it is shared or exported.

documents.title: Endorse and certify trusted content
documents.content: Endorsement helps consumers identify trusted analytics assets. Promote useful content and certify authoritative items through a review process with clear ownership and quality standards.

documents.title: Track lineage and impact
documents.content: Lineage shows how sources, pipelines, lakehouses, semantic models, and reports are connected. Use impact analysis before changes to identify downstream consumers.

documents.title: Monitor activity and audit usage
documents.content: Monitor sharing, viewing, creation, refresh, and administrative events to understand adoption, verify policy, and investigate unusual behavior.

category: Prepare and process data in Fabric

documents.title: Design data ingestion
documents.content: Consider data volume, latency, schema, full or incremental loading, security, and the needs of downstream lakehouse, warehouse, and Power BI consumers.

documents.title: Choose an ingestion tool
documents.content: Choose Dataflow Gen2 for low-code transformations, pipelines or copy jobs for repeatable movement, notebooks for code-driven processing, and eventstreams for real-time events.

documents.title: Load data into a lakehouse
documents.content: Load raw files for flexible processing or write curated Delta tables for reliable SQL, Spark, Direct Lake, and downstream analytics access.

documents.title: Load data into a warehouse
documents.content: Fabric warehouses support relational ingestion with pipelines, dataflows, cross-database queries, and T-SQL. Preserve keys, data types, and transaction behavior.

documents.title: Build Dataflow Gen2 transformations
documents.content: Dataflow Gen2 uses Power Query for visual data preparation. Connect to sources, set types, filter and combine data, preserve query folding, and write to Fabric destinations.

documents.title: Transform data with notebooks
documents.content: Fabric notebooks support interactive Spark development with Python, SQL, Scala, and R for exploration, cleansing, transformation, machine learning, and Delta table operations.

documents.title: Transform data with T-SQL
documents.content: Use T-SQL queries, views, stored procedures, and table operations in warehouses and SQL analytics endpoints to create repeatable business-ready structures.

documents.title: Build data pipelines
documents.content: Combine copy, notebook, dataflow, script, and control-flow activities with parameters and dependencies to build reusable Fabric workflows.

documents.title: Process incremental changes
documents.content: Track a watermark or change feed, identify inserted, updated, and deleted records, and apply idempotent upserts to process changes efficiently.

documents.title: Process real-time events
documents.content: Use eventstreams to route events, eventhouses and KQL databases to store them, and KQL querysets or dashboards to investigate live and historical patterns.

documents.title: Profile and clean data
documents.content: Profiling reveals distributions, missing values, invalid types, and duplicates. Define explicit rules for rejected, corrected, or quarantined data.

documents.title: Design a medallion architecture
documents.content: Bronze preserves source data, silver validates and standardizes it, and gold presents modeled business data for reporting and analysis.

documents.title: Validate data quality
documents.content: Validate schemas, nullability, uniqueness, ranges, relationships, and business rules, then log and handle failures consistently.

category: Model and visualize data with Power BI

documents.title: Design a star schema
documents.content: Separate measurable facts from descriptive dimensions. Define a clear grain, stable keys, and appropriate relationships to make semantic models understandable and efficient.

documents.title: Create model relationships
documents.content: Configure cardinality, cross-filter direction, and active relationships carefully, favoring simple one-to-many paths that avoid ambiguity.

documents.title: Choose a semantic model storage mode
documents.content: Choose Import for in-memory speed, DirectQuery for source-based queries, Direct Lake for OneLake data, or a composite design when requirements differ by table.

documents.title: Create DAX measures
documents.content: DAX measures calculate results in the current filter context. Build explicit reusable measures and use CALCULATE when you need to modify context.

documents.title: Implement time intelligence
documents.content: Use a complete date table with suitable relationships and DAX calculations for year-to-date, prior-period, and rolling-window analysis.

documents.title: Optimize semantic model performance
documents.content: Remove unnecessary columns, choose compact data types, simplify relationships and DAX, and use diagnostic tools to locate bottlenecks.

documents.title: Configure incremental refresh
documents.content: Incremental refresh partitions large tables by time so only recent data is refreshed routinely. Configure date parameters and preserve query folding.

documents.title: Design effective Power BI reports
documents.content: Select visuals that match analytical tasks, maintain a consistent layout and hierarchy, and reduce decoration that competes with the data.

documents.title: Add interactive report navigation
documents.content: Use slicers, drillthrough, report page tooltips, bookmarks, and buttons to help users move predictably from overview to detail.

documents.title: Build accessible reports
documents.content: Provide meaningful titles and alt text, logical tab order, sufficient contrast, keyboard-friendly navigation, and cues that do not rely on color alone.

documents.title: Publish and share Power BI content
documents.content: Publish reports and semantic models to a managed workspace, then distribute curated content through a Power BI app with suitable audiences and permissions.

documents.title: Use Git integration
documents.content: Connect development workspaces to branches, review changes through pull requests, and synchronize supported Fabric items carefully to avoid overwriting work.

documents.title: Use deployment pipelines
documents.content: Promote supported Fabric and Power BI content through development, test, and production stages. Compare stages and validate dependencies after each promotion.

documents.title: Test Fabric analytics solutions
documents.content: Test transformation logic, data quality, pipeline integration, semantic model calculations, security roles, report behavior, and business acceptance.

documents.title: Monitor Fabric capacity
documents.content: Use the Fabric Capacity Metrics app to identify overloaded periods, expensive items, throttling, and opportunities to reschedule, optimize, or resize.

documents.title: Monitor pipelines and refreshes
documents.content: Use the Monitoring hub and item histories to investigate failed pipelines, notebooks, dataflows, and semantic model refreshes before retrying them.

documents.title: What is Microsoft Fabric?
documents.content: Microsoft Fabric is a unified analytics platform for data integration, engineering, warehousing, real-time analytics, data science, governance, and business intelligence.

documents.title: What is OneLake?
documents.content: OneLake is the organization-wide logical data lake built into Fabric. It provides common storage for Fabric items and reduces copies through shared open-format data and shortcuts.

documents.title: What is Power BI?
documents.content: Power BI is the business intelligence experience in Fabric. It supports data preparation, semantic modeling, interactive visualization, sharing, and governed consumption.

documents.title: What is a semantic model?
documents.content: A semantic model presents data through tables, relationships, measures, hierarchies, and business-friendly metadata so reports use consistent definitions.

documents.title: What is Direct Lake?
documents.content: Direct Lake is a semantic model storage mode that queries supported OneLake data with minimal duplication and interactive performance.

documents.title: How Fabric and Power BI work together
documents.content: Fabric prepares, stores, processes, and governs data while Power BI models and presents it. Shared workspaces, security, lineage, and OneLake connect the experiences.
